timeline.title: The First Page
timeline.text: Somewhere in this year, an ordinary conversation happened. Neither of us knew it was the first page.

timeline.title: Becoming Friends
timeline.text: Small talk retired early. In its place: book arguments, inside jokes, and the discovery that silence with the right person is its own language.

timeline.title: The Chapters In Between
timeline.text: Exams, doubts, growing pains — and through all of it, the conversations kept finding their way back.

timeline.title: The Distance Test
timeline.text: The world went quiet; the friendship didn't. Voice notes, late-night calls, and the stubborn refusal to let a good thing gather dust.

timeline.title: The Becoming Years
timeline.text: You started turning into the person children smile at before opening their mouths. I mostly just watched, impressed and unsurprised.

timeline.title: Still Here
timeline.text: More books. More chai. More 'It's my destiny.' The archive kept growing without either of us trying.

timeline.title: The Permanent Collection
timeline.text: Still collecting. The museum's acquisition department reports no plans to stop.

memoryCards.text: The first conversation. Not because it was extraordinary. Because neither of us knew it was the first page.
The first time I realised — "You're different."
The first time you made me laugh so hard I still remember it.
The first birthday I celebrated with you.

mirrorLines: You genuinely become happier around books.
You remember little details about people, even when you pretend not to.
Your smile isn't ordinary. It never was.
You're kinder than your own description of yourself.
You carry more than you tell anyone.
You make quiet rooms feel safer.
You keep showing up. That's rarer than you think.

observations.text: You genuinely become happier around books.
You call yourself difficult. But the people who love you never describe you that way.
You remember little details about people. Even when you pretend not to.
You carry more than you tell anyone.
When life gets overwhelming... you disappear instead of asking for help.
You apologise for existing more than you should.
You trust slowly. But once you do... you trust completely.
You think your smile is ordinary. It isn't.
You think your life isn't interesting. Meanwhile... someone built an entire museum from it.

secretObservation.title: One More Thing.
secretObservation.text: You never really realise the effect you have on people. Maybe that's why kindness comes so naturally to you.

performances.title: The First Performance
performances.description: The lights were too bright and the music started half a beat early. None of it mattered once you began.
performances.memory: You said you were nervous. Nobody in the audience could tell.
performances.curatorNote: Archived from memory. The recording is imperfect; the moment was not.

performances.title: The One With The Red Dupatta
performances.description: A classical piece that somehow made a crowded hall feel completely silent.
performances.memory: The spin at the end — the whole row stood up. You didn't see it. You never looked at the audience.

performances.title: The Living Room Rehearsal
performances.description: Lockdown edition. Furniture pushed aside. A phone propped against a stack of books served as the only camera.
performances.memory: Proof that a stage is optional. The dancing never was.
performances.curatorNote: The most honest recording in this collection.

performances.title: The Wedding Sangeet Surprise

performances.memory: Aunties asked for choreography lessons afterwards. You laughed for ten minutes.

performances.title: The One She Doesn't Know I Saved

envelopeText: You once asked me why I notice so many little things about you.
Because you've spent years quietly becoming one of the people I pay the most attention to.
And somewhere along the way, noticing stopped being something I tried to do.

mapPins.memory: Funny how ordinary places become landmarks once enough memories happen there.
The bill, the photo, the conversation, what you ordered — all archived. The inside joke stays classified.
Books bought, recommendations exchanged, wallets harmed. We are no longer allowed to make eye contact with the bestseller table.
Routes traced between cities, each stop with its own photos and little stories. The best wrong turns in recorded history.

gallery10.brightestStarText: The brightest memories usually felt completely ordinary while they were happening.

letters.title: If I Had Said This Earlier
body: There are sentences I drafted a hundred times and never sent. Most of them were just this: I noticed. I always noticed.
The way you show up tired and still show up. The way you make caring look accidental.
If I had said this earlier, maybe you'd have believed it sooner. So here it is now, in ink, where it can't be unsaid.

letters.title: When I Was Proud Of You
body: Every exam you passed while insisting you'd fail. Every patient who left your chair less afraid than they arrived.
I never made a speech about it. You'd have hated a speech.
But for the record, kept safely in this museum: I was proud. Loudly, silently proud.

letters.title: When You Thought You Failed
body: You called it failure. I watched the same event and saw someone getting back up before the dust settled.
You blamed destiny that day. I still think it was bad luck.
Either way — you kept going. This letter exists so that version of you is never forgotten.

letters.title: When You Didn't Believe Yourself
body: You have a habit of trusting everyone's judgment except your own.
So borrow mine: you are more capable than your worst day told you.
Keep this letter for the next time you forget. Knowing you, that's soon.

letters.title: When You Called Yourself Difficult
body: You said it like a confession. Like a warning label.
But the people who love you have never once used that word.
Careful is not difficult. Guarded is not difficult. You are not difficult. You are worth the patience — and it isn't even that much patience.

letters.title: When You Trusted Me
body: I know what trust costs you. I know it isn't given — it's lent, carefully, and watched.
So when you handed it over, I understood what I was holding.
I still do. Some locks protect what's inside. Thank you for opening this one.

letters.title: When You Were Quiet
body: Your silences have dialects. I've learned most of them.
The tired one. The overwhelmed one. The one that means 'ask me again, gently.'
For all the times I read them right — good. For the times I missed — this letter is the apology.

letters.title: When I Wanted To Make You Smile
body: Which was often. Which was always, honestly.
Every bad joke, every meme sent at surgical timing, every 'read this' — all of it had one job.
Your real smile — the one you think is ordinary — was worth every terrible pun it cost.

letters.title: When We Didn't Talk
body: There were gaps. Life does that.
But the friendship never felt paused to me — just quietly holding its page, like a bookmark.
We always picked up mid-sentence. We always will.

letters.title: On Your Birthday
body: Every year I try to find the words, and every year they come out as cake and bad singing.
This year they came out as a museum.
Happy Birthday, Chicko. The exhibits were never about the past. They were about you.

letters.title: For Every Version of You I Haven't Met Yet
body: To the you of next year, and the one after: I hope you're still reading too many books.
I hope you've stopped apologising for existing. I hope you trust a little faster — or don't, and stay exactly as careful as you are.
Whoever you become, this museum has already reserved a wing.

letters.title: Always
body: No occasion for this one. No date. No reason.
Just the standing fact, filed under permanent records:
Whatever chapter, whatever year, whatever mood — always.

epilogueLines: Some museums are built to preserve history.
This one was built to remember gratitude.
Thank you for unknowingly leaving so many beautiful things behind.
postCreditsLetter: Museums usually preserve history. This one was never really about history.
It was about gratitude. About all the ordinary conversations, random jokes, books, difficult days, tiny victories, and little moments that quietly became part of my life because you were there.
You once told me that memories fade. Maybe they do.

That's exactly why I built this place. Not so we'd never forget. But so that years from now, if either of us ever wondered whether those ordinary moments mattered... there would be somewhere we could come back to and smile.

rules: Feel free to revisit your favourite exhibits.
The exit exists. The memories don't.
dearChickoLetter: If you're reading this... then congratulations.
None of these exhibits exist because I wanted to remember everything. They exist because you made ordinary moments worth remembering.
Don't worry. Entry is free. Photography is allowed. Smiling is encouraged. Crying... also allowed.
Over the next few rooms you'll see photographs, conversations, books, tiny moments, and memories. Most of them probably seemed ordinary when they happened.
That's the funny thing about ordinary moments. You rarely realize they're becoming memories.
This museum isn't here to tell you who you are. You already know that better than anyone.
It's simply here to show you what it looked like from where I was standing.
So... take your time. Look closely. Some exhibits are louder than others. Some are hiding. And a few... only appear if you're curious enough to find them.
